paragraphs: On Monday, Mia had a geography project for Teacher Kim's class. She had to prepare a talk about the rivers and the mountains of Thailand. Her small suitcase had a map, a smooth stone, and a green shell. That morning, Mia's throat was sore, and she felt worried. Lily saw her face and gave her a bottle of water. "Are you all right?" asked Lily. "My throat hurts, and I am worried," said Mia.

Mia went to Nurse Jill before the lesson. "Your throat is a little red," said Nurse Jill. "Drink some warm water, and rest your voice." Mia drank the warm water, and then she walked back to the class. It was frightening to stand in front of twenty children. Her hands were cold, and her voice was very small.

Mia began her talk, but nobody could hear the end of it. She stopped and looked at the floor. Nobody laughed. Teacher Kim waited and did not speak. "Good try, Mia," said Teacher Kim kindly. "Your map is very nice, and your words are clear." "Now speak a little louder, and look at your friends." "Touch the map when you say the name of a river." "Then begin again." Lily smiled at Mia from her seat.

Mia took a deep breath and began again. This time, she touched the map and said, "This is a long river." Her voice was louder, and she looked at her friends. She showed the smooth stone and the green shell from her suitcase. "This shell comes from a river," she said. The class listened, and nobody made a noise. Mia felt strong now.

At the end, the children clapped their hands. "Well done, Mia," said Teacher Kim. "The second talk was much better than the first one." Mia smiled, and her throat did not feel so sore. "I was worried," she told Lily after the lesson, "but now I am happy."
text.summary: Mia has a sore throat on the day of her geography talk. Teacher Kim gives her simple feedback, and Mia feels better and finishes her talk with a small suitcase of things.
